title: Corneal crosslinking efficacy in patients with keratoconus under 18 years of age

license.statement: CC BY, version not stated (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution License; no licence URL in the XML)

groups.description: Epithelium-off corneal collagen cross-linking by the Dresden protocol (8-10 mm epithelial removal, 0.1% riboflavin-5-phosphate with 20% dextran T-500, 370 nm UVA 3 mW/cm2 for 30 min) for progressive keratoconus in patients under 18 years; 12 eyes of 10 patients, one surgeon, private clinic, 2013-2018, chart review. Inclusion required attendance at all semiannual appointments and at least 2 years of postoperative follow-up; eyes with intrastromal ring implants and patients who missed follow-ups were excluded. Procedure described as cross-linking only (no cataract surgery).

exclusions.reason: figure; the tabulated values are used

exclusions.what: Text statement of lines of vision gained

notes: Kmax, pachymetry, foveal thickness, uncorrected distance visual acuity and endothelial cell density (Tables 2-3) are mentioned here only.

The inclusion criterion (all semiannual appointments and at least 2 years of follow-up) is a minimum follow-up shorter than the last tabulated visit; fewer eyes at the 36-60-month visits are kept as ordinary attrition.

series.notes: Mean ± SD (Methods: numerical variables presented as mean ± standard deviation); unit logMAR (Methods: 'visual acuity with and without correction (logMAR)'). Table 2 (Pre, 6, 12, 18, 24 months) and Table 3 (36, 42, 48, 54, 60 months) report the same 12-eye group. Table 3 footnote: the 60-month value is from one eye; the 54-month cell has no data and is omitted; other per-visit numbers of eyes are not reported.
